title: See what you will build
why: A file is easier to understand when you know its job in the game.
outcome: Explain what a Match does and where each part runs.

checks.expected: Run checks visible examples without scoring. Submit uses hidden tests. The server owns the score.

failure.symptom: Run and Submit still feel the same
failure.diagnostic: Compare which tests each action can use.
failure.meaning: Visible examples help you practice; hidden tests decide the score.

steps.title: Start with the destination
steps.question: What are we building?
explanation: Code Arena is a game where two sides solve the same programming Problem. A side is one player in 1v1, or two teammates in 2v2.
One Match contains three Rounds in the reference game. Each Round brings a new Problem. You will build the pieces in a separate practice folder before connecting them to your team’s app.

steps.title: Follow one Round
steps.question: What does a player do?
explanation: Read the Problem. Write a small program in the editor. Run the visible examples to find mistakes. Submit when you want the hidden tests to score your code.
At Reveal, both sides see the Round results. After the last Round, the game adds the scores and decides the winner.

steps.title: Give each part one job
steps.question: Where does the work happen?
explanation: The browser shows the editor and results. The server checks who may act and keeps the official Match state. The database saves accepted state.
A separate Judge runs player programs inside an isolated environment. Your browser and the Game server must not execute untrusted player code directly.

vocabulary.meaning: A running program that receives requests and owns the official game rules.

steps.title: Predict a change
steps.question: Does pressing Run increase the score?
explanation: Predict the answer before opening the hints. Run uses visible examples and never changes the score.
A helpful example: checking your answers on a practice sheet is different from handing in an exam.

steps.title: Draw your first game map
steps.question: Can you give each part its job?
explanation: On paper or in the note box, draw four labeled boxes: Browser, Server, Database, Judge. Put the editor under Browser and official score under Server.
Do not create a code repository yet. The next lessons show exactly where your practice files will go.
